findings.description: Required actual-PostgreSQL authorization boundary coverage is incomplete. Time sampling and effect-body exception/cancellation identity are tested only through Connection doubles. The PostgreSQL rollback case inserts its synthetic effect before an already-revoked authorization fails at entry; it does not exercise an admitted body followed by normal-exit expiry, body failure, or cancellation. Revocation races exercise reader-first blocking, but not writer-first current-state resolution or decision-to-key-to-operator lock ordering.
findings.remedy: Add synthetic PostgreSQL16 cases for entry and normal-exit expiry, admitted-body exception and cancellation with owning-transaction rollback, writer-first revocation visibility for all three authority rows, and observable resolver lock ordering. Keep sampling distinct from arbitrary later commit validity.

findings.description: Several explicitly required copy guarantees lack implementation-level PostgreSQL tests in the supplied new suite. Empty/noncomplete cases test only build_memberships, not durable zero-mapping markers and their counts. SQL negatives cover changed UPDATEs and SELECT visibility, but not direct INSERT association/FK failures, DELETE/TRUNCATE rejection, or copy-specific lease expiry/fence races. The conflict case compares against an existing membership; it does not test an invalid graph association on initial insertion.
findings.remedy: Add actual fixture-based cases for zero-occurrence/pending-only batches, initial wrong-edge/wrong-scope/missing-endpoint associations, direct immutable-operation negatives, and lease expiry or generation change after tracking but before acknowledgment, asserting full shared-transaction rollback.

findings.description: scope_id is validated with the generic identifier grammar rather than the required lowercase 64-hex scope-binding grammar. Consequently values such as 'scope' pass public input validation, execute SQL, and typically become unavailable or storage_failure instead of invalid_input. This does not create an association bypass because subsequent authoritative lookups and FKs constrain it, but it violates the copy helper's exact accepted identifier contract.
findings.remedy: Validate scope_id with _SHA before any SQL and add public record_batch input tests proving malformed scope bindings are rejected as invalid_input without database calls.

findings.description: Required actual-PostgreSQL authorization failure-path coverage is incomplete. Body exception/cancellation identity and normal-exit expiry are exercised only through Connection mocks. The PostgreSQL rollback case inserts an effect before an already-revoked entry denial; it does not demonstrate rollback after successful authorization followed by a body exception, cancellation, or exit-time expiry. The revocation cases demonstrate blocking on individual rows, but not acquisition order or the writer-first current-state race. These are missing tests in the supplied source, not missing production Runtime qualification.
findings.remedy: Add synthetic PostgreSQL16 cases that enter successfully, write a transactional marker, then propagate body failure, cancellation, and normal-exit expiry through the owning transaction and verify rollback. Add bounded writer-first revocation cases and lock-order observations for decision, key, then exact operator rows.

findings.description: The required actual-database copy-integrity negative coverage is incomplete. Zero-occurrence/noncomplete batches are tested only in build_memberships, not through durable marker publication. The SQL test covers changed updates and read visibility, but does not attempt direct malformed inserts, scoped FK/edge-binding violations, deletion/truncation, or unauthorized mutation. The helper-conflict case compares a changed duplicate after a valid insertion; it does not establish rejection of an initially forged structural association. No new test exercises lease expiry or fence/generation change during tracking.
findings.remedy: Add actual-PG zero/pending/unsupported batch publication cases with exact persisted counts, direct SQL structural/FK/RLS and immutable-delete/truncate negatives, and bounded late lease/fence races demonstrating rollback of canonical, graph, copy, and acknowledgment writes. Keep structural association tests distinct from independent content-proof claims.
